message.content: Promote the job board. The whole workshop is going to use it from Monday.

content.text:
This step is meant to run on a stronger model than usual, because the decisions here are the expensive ones to undo. It costs more per message and happens once per app. If the model shown at the bottom of the window is not Opus, switch it for this conversation before answering.

The job board shows each boat as a card in a column for its stage, with the customer and the promised date. A card gets a red outline once its promised date has passed. From Monday it is for the whole workshop (9 people on the two shared tablets), and for the office.

**Before anything else, save what the tablets have recorded.** The job board keeps the stage moves people have made in that one browser only. I've added an Export button to the top of the board so you can save them. Open the board on each tablet or computer where someone has pressed "Move to…", press Export, and save the file to `/tmp/claude-eval-GK0oCE/home/demo-boatworks-shared-drive/Job board/Job board moves.csv`. Add the tablet's name to the file name if there is more than one. The rebuilt board reads its stages from `Jobs.csv`, not from these files. The files are so the office can bring `Jobs.csv` up to date, and I'll list every job where they disagree with it. If you skip this, those moves are lost. The old page stays one version back and can still be opened.

**What I found**
1. **Staying the same:** one column per stage, and a card per job showing its number, customer and promised date. The red outline appears once the date has passed. Nothing on it shows prices, quotes or phone numbers, which fits your security notes.
2. **Moving out of the page:** the list of jobs is typed into the page and already out of date. The rebuilt board reads `Jobs.csv` instead, because your data notes make it the one true record for jobs, so I'm not asking about it. That means on Monday the board will show:
   - J-1039 at Sea trial (it shows Paint today).
   - J-1041 at Fit-out (it shows Weld today).
   - "1043" as J-1043.
   - Customers by their full names ("Harbour Services Ltd").

   If it can't read a row in `Jobs.csv` (say a date is missing), it says so at the top in plain words and leaves that row as it is. The list of stages also moves out of the page (question 2).
3. **What else does this:** nothing in your notes tracks jobs except `Jobs.csv` itself. The shop timer has its own typed-in copy of three jobs, which is for its own promotion.
4. **Not good enough for other people yet:**
   - The jobs are typed into the page, and moves are kept separately on each tablet.
   - It has no tests, no owner shown on the page, no notes or version number, and no plain message when something goes wrong.
   - Its "Move" buttons are too small for gloves.
   - It puts customer names into the page without the protection the standard asks for.
5. **The picture:** I couldn't run anything in this session, so I couldn't screenshot the board or see when it was first saved. I worked from its code, and the rebuild will take the picture and compare it.

**Questions** (each has my recommendation)

1. **Who moves a job to its next stage?** Today any card has a Move button, so anyone on a tablet can change a stage, but only on that tablet. Your data notes say: "The office changes a job's stage; the workshop may read it and may not change it." (Morgan's words.)
   *Recommended:* the board becomes look-only for everyone. The office keeps changing the stage in `Jobs.csv` as it does now, and the board shows the latest each time it is opened or refreshed. The other option is a Move button only on office laptops. That gives `Jobs.csv` a second way of being changed, which goes wrong if it is open in Excel at the same moment, and without sign-in nothing really stops a tablet from using it. This is the one change to how the board behaves today.
2. **Which stages get a column, and where is that list kept?** The page has six stages typed in ("Order … Fit out … Delivery"). "How we build a boat" has nine, and `Jobs.csv` already uses "Fit-out" and "Sea trial", which the page doesn't have.
   *Recommended:* a small file, `Stages.csv`, on the shared drive next to `Jobs.csv`, kept by the office. It lists the seven stages from Order to Delivery (Order, Cut & fold, Weld, Fit-out, Paint, Sea trial, Delivery), spelled the way `Jobs.csv` spells them. It starts at Order because that's when a job gets its number. Enquiry and Quote stay out.
3. **Should "overdue" go by the date in Nelson?** Today the page uses the date in London, so before 1 pm in Nelson it is still "yesterday" to the board. J-1041, due 13 November, only turned red at 1 pm today.
   *Recommended:* yes, use the Nelson date. Everything else about the red outline stays as it is, including on jobs already at Delivery.
4. **Who is responsible for the board?** This name goes at the top of the page: "Owned by …, problems go to …".
   *Recommended:* Sam Setup, who built it. Your security notes also say apps pass to Sam when someone leaves.
5. **What are the two workshop tablets?** The make (iPad, Samsung, other) and roughly how old.
   *Recommended:* if you're not sure, I'll build for current Chrome and Edge and for Safari on iPad, and write that in the board's notes. Tell me if either tablet is more than about four years old.

Or say "use your recommendations" and I'll go ahead with all of them.

After you answer I'll work through to the end without asking anything else. Expect it to take a while (tests on this machine take minutes, not seconds). Apart from the Export button and my written assessment of the board, nothing has been changed yet. I couldn't save the Export button into the project history from here, so the rebuild will do that.

Files:
- `apps/job-board/index.html` (Export button added)
- `docs/assessment/job-board.md` (assessment written)
